review_kind: project-provided review and independent agent recheck; not external peer review
interpretation: Addressed means the specified correction was made and its stated check performed. Clarified means the evidence or scope required a reasoned correction to the proposed change. Neither label asserts deployed implementation, authenticated historical runs or general validity.

findings.title: Chain-preservation proposition is false as stated
findings.response: Replaced the false chain statement with explicit per-step partial-correctness contracts, next-step precondition compatibility, and equality of adjacent observation functions on intermediate postconditions. Added both Boolean countermodels and an induction proof.
verification: Both omitted-junction counterexamples are executable in tools/test_reviewed_formal_results.py.
15,840 endpoint witnesses satisfy the corrected premises in the declared two-state relational enumeration.
findings.remaining_limit: The finite controls supplement the written proof; neither verifies a natural-language transformation implementation.

findings.title: The central reuse theorem never connects the verified properties to the new request
findings.response: Made every verified property request-indexed, required equal complete state and request observations, and explicitly partitioned the complete new requirement set into property-covered artifact conditions and separately checked current-use conditions. The conclusion now follows through both groups rather than from state equality alone.
verification: Executable countermodels show preserved old properties missing an added requirement and stable state with a changed request referent.
20,480 output witnesses satisfy request coverage, preservation, and current-use conditions in the declared finite model.
Coordinated matching restatement with the studies editor.
findings.remaining_limit: Completeness of dependencies and new requirements, soundness of verification, and the coverage implication remain explicit assumptions; the theorem does not discover them.

findings.title: Idempotence proposition omits serialization of concurrent duplicates, and the stored result
findings.response: Required serialization or an equivalent unique first-commit constraint for each event identifier, and atomic persistence of the payload fingerprint, result or stable result reference, identifier, and internal effect. Explained loser rollback and why independent atomic commits are insufficient.
verification: Re-read the proof against the concurrent-first-delivery counterexample and the stored-result obligation.
findings.remaining_limit: No deployed concurrency implementation or external exactly-once execution is claimed.

findings.title: Generation-admission result assumes generation identifiers are never reused
findings.response: Generation identifiers are never reissued within a Work Item, including rollback and restoration of earlier requirement text. The direct-admission comparison occurs at the acceptance transition's serialization point.
verification: Checked the proof against a return-to-earlier-content scenario; content hashes alone are explicitly insufficient.
findings.remaining_limit: The result assumes the interpreter identifies material requirement changes and the transition enforces the identifier rule.

findings.title: "Retention" is used against the glossary and the reuse-policy specification
findings.response: Renamed the paper to Knowledge Utility, Resource Accounting, and Lifecycle Decisions; reserved retention for byte preservation/deletion and separated residency, search visibility, background preparation, and current-use eligibility.
verification: Checked every retention occurrence against its storage-policy sense; coordinated glossary terminology.
findings.remaining_limit: The model specifies no universal retention threshold or utility-based authority to delete an original.

findings.title: Applicability uses three verdict values, but the status model has four
findings.response: Aligned the applicability model with pass/fail/unknown/not_applicable and defined discharge as pass or a justified scope-specific exemption witness. Added the empty-requirement-set vacuity and requirement-completeness limitation; updated the strengthening proof to keep witnesses and discharge semantics fixed.
verification: Compared the four values and guarded exemption meaning with the status-model editor; checked the monotonic subset proof under fixed witnesses.
findings.remaining_limit: A bare not_applicable label and an empty or incomplete requirement set supply no independent assurance.

findings.title: The cited study does not cover the transition properties it is linked to
findings.response: Narrowed the projection-study link to reader boundaries, addressed revision selection, and partial projections. Explicitly states that no engineering study in this corpus tests Work Item generations or concurrent idempotence.
verification: Read the linked projection-study methods and evidence boundary.
findings.remaining_limit: Generation and concurrency implementation studies remain unperformed; this is disclosed rather than replaced with invented evidence.

findings.title: The transcription study is described as addressing alternative readings and source regions
findings.response: Described the transcription study as a loss/restoration of recorded uncertainty in a reproducible projection. Explicitly excluded plural-interpretation and source-locator correctness claims from that study's evidence.
verification: Read the transcription-study audit, uncertainty projection, and reproduction limits.
findings.remaining_limit: The proposed plural-reading and locator obligations have not been evaluated by the published studies.

findings.title: The dependency-closure study is credited with selection controls it excludes
findings.response: Restricted the closure-study pointer to all-required fixed-graph closure, historical layout, and preliminary delivery. Distinguished root-subset enumeration from budgeted composition and identified the untested alternative-group and optimization claims.
verification: Read the closure profile's all operator and rejection of alternative-choice/cyclic inputs; audited the remaining scientific-to-study pointers.
findings.remaining_limit: No executable selection study for alternative grounds or resource-constrained optimization is asserted.

findings.title: The "central falsifiable engineering prediction" is true by definition
findings.response: Replaced the definitional enforcement conditional with a falsifiable claim about a named implementation revision, a well-formed input domain that includes violations, and a concrete mandatory condition. Added separate positive controls so all-refusal behavior is not mistaken for usefulness.
verification: Checked that a violating input receiving success refutes the displayed formula without assuming enforcement.
findings.remaining_limit: The formula is a protocol for testing a specified implementation, not a claim that a particular live service already satisfies it.

findings.title: Notation clash in the break-even result and against the study it accompanies
findings.response: Kept h for the observation horizon; used G for cold cost, B preparation, N requests, and c_hit for total admitted-hit cost. Mapped the simple theorem to the study model at rho=1, M=I=S=0 and c_hit=c_v+c_r, with a common horizon and cost scope.
verification: Algebraically checked B+N*c_hit < N*G iff N*(G-c_hit)>B; coordinated the study's c_v/c_r/rho notation.
findings.remaining_limit: The arithmetic remains analytical and assumes the same acceptance conditions and accounting scope.

findings.title: Unscoped "complete" claims
findings.response: Removed unscoped completeness claims from the transformation and revision papers. Replaced them with the specific conditional properties and distinctions actually developed.
verification: Checked both flagged passages and nearby scope qualifications.
findings.remaining_limit: Neither paper claims to enumerate every transformation or governance model.

findings.title: Soundness proposition ignores the side conditions the paper itself records
findings.response: Added satisfaction of every inference application's side conditions to the finite-derivation theorem and its induction step, with the nonzero-divisor condition as a simple boundary example.
verification: Checked that a conditionally sound rule cannot support the induction when a required side condition is false.
findings.remaining_limit: Extraction correctness, model adequacy, and implementation compliance remain separate assumptions.

findings.title: Adoption argument assumes a countermodel exists
findings.response: Made the adoption argument explicitly about a factual proposition for which the adoption record is consistent with both it and its negation. Excluded tautologies and facts entailed by the adoption record itself.
verification: Verified the countermodel argument from satisfiability of A and not-F; checked the stated exclusions.
findings.remaining_limit: A separate truth-linked review procedure may add evidence, but its reliability is not supplied by adoption alone.

findings.title: The same reverse-reachability proposition appears twice under different wording
findings.response: Kept the general reverse-reachability proposition in revision-and-governance, retitled it as identification of reassessment candidates, and replaced the duplicate interaction proof with a linked application. Renumbered the remaining narrow-update proposition in interaction from 4 to 3.
verification: Publication parser resolves the new cross-paper fragment.
The current corpus has 23 distinct numbered formal statements after removing the duplicate.
findings.remaining_limit: Candidate identification does not prove that an affected output is false or that every semantic dependency was recorded.

findings.title: The reuse theorem's transformation is a function, but the transformation paper uses relations; verification correctness is assumed silently
findings.response: Expressed reuse transformation as a relation and required preservation for every permitted transformation output. Prior verified properties must actually hold; a positive receipt is not assumed sound merely because it exists. Added an explicit no-existence/no-termination boundary.
verification: Executable controls distinguish one good relational output from universal output preservation and a recorded pass from actual prior truth.
findings.remaining_limit: The current-use admission is a derived conclusion; the transformation premise does not presuppose it.

findings.title: "Conservative allocation prevents creation of cost" allows negative shares
findings.response: Recast shared-cost allocation over a finite set of operations with nonnegative costs, consumer shares, and residuals. The proof now both conserves the aggregate and rules out an excessive positive share offset by a negative share.
verification: Checked the finite sum identity and the per-share bound from nonnegativity.
findings.remaining_limit: This remains an accounting identity, not a uniquely fair allocation rule.

findings.title: Contribution target compares against \(\pi_b\), while attribution requires \(\pi\)
findings.response: Defined scalar outcome mapping U, made artifact-specific attribution compare pi+k with pi, and reserved comparison with pi_b for a whole-policy contrast. Introduced V_set for set-valued interventions under the same fixed conditioning arguments.
verification: Checked that the displayed contrast isolates only the declared artifact-access intervention; no automatic identification from observational logs is claimed.
findings.remaining_limit: Assignment, interference, population support, and measurement assumptions are still needed for a causal estimate.

findings.title: The downward-closure counterexample conflicts with the paper's closure-based support definition
findings.response: Replaced the inconsistent root-removal example with a one-requirement/no-dependency coverage example: {a} is feasible and the empty subset is not. Explained separately that removing a root-level dependency may leave closure unchanged, whereas removing it from delivered content can violate delivery.
verification: Evaluated the example under the paper's actual Supports(r,A) definition with closure equal to A.
findings.remaining_limit: The distinction concerns selected roots versus actual delivered objects; it does not establish a general optimization algorithm.

findings.title: Proof step attributed to submodularity also uses monotonicity
findings.response: Attributed OPT <= f(A_i union O) to monotonicity and the sum-of-marginals bound to submodularity, preserving the normalized monotone/cardinality hypotheses.
verification: Re-read the recurrence argument with each inequality's premise explicit.
findings.remaining_limit: The bound is not extended to arbitrary budgets, dependency closure, or non-submodular semantic value.

findings.title: The Boolean residual example shows reconstruction, not economy
findings.response: Added that residual reconstruction proves correctness rather than economy, since R_F=F is also a valid residual. Any size or compression claim requires its own measure and comparison.
verification: Checked C and F equals F under F entails C, for the alternative residual.
findings.remaining_limit: No compression ratio or useful common-theme extraction is claimed.

findings.title: The papers do not cite the corpus's own counterexample to closure minimality
findings.response: Linked the corpus's actual claim-level minimality counterexample immediately after least entity closure and from the composition model. Distinguished least vertices/edges from least claims or token cost.
verification: Read the projection-study counterexample and resolved its fragment using the publication parser.
findings.remaining_limit: The retained original experiment scores and entity-level theorem are unchanged; only the overbroad inference is excluded.

findings.title: The closure proposition permits cycles, but the cited implementation rejects them
findings.response: Explicitly states that cycles are allowed by the set-theoretic fixed-point proof but rejected by the published engineering profile. The executable evidence supports that acyclic profile only.
verification: Compared the proof with the closure-study's cycle rejection rule.
findings.remaining_limit: The cyclic case is proof-supported, not empirically established by the cited consumer.

findings.title: Prior work that the papers' results restate without citation
findings.response: Verified the five proposed prior works against original articles, author/institutional copies, or publisher records before citation. Added scoped connections for program slicing, truth maintenance, incremental builds, view complements, and AGM revision, with explicit differences from task-relative knowledge admission.
verification: Primary-source URLs, verified metadata, inspected portions, and proposed source-register paths are recorded in papers-prior-work.json.
Five entries supplied to the reference editor; source-register integration supplied to root.
findings.remaining_limit: This is targeted verification of these additions, not a systematic related-work review or a new audit of every pre-existing bibliography item.

findings.title: Utility paper points to "measured workloads" in a study that reports none
findings.response: Replaced the measured-workloads pointer with an exact description of finite admission controls and synthetic arithmetic, explicitly stating that the study reports no measured model savings or production workload.
verification: Compared the pointer against the companion study's analytical scope.
findings.remaining_limit: The editorial setting is separately described as exploratory and without a cost estimate.

findings.title: Notation reuse within and across papers
findings.response: Renamed the semantic-objects selected-root set to Roots so R remains requirements, removed the in-paper h clash, and coordinated a scoped mathematical-symbol registry with the glossary editor. Different locally defined symbols across papers are documented rather than silently equated.
verification: Checked root-set replacements through the closure construction and proof; coordinated common cost notation and glossary scope table.
findings.remaining_limit: The corpus does not impose one universal meaning on every single-letter symbol; definitions and paper scope determine meaning.

findings.title: Rights guard bypassed through the knowledge layer; licence and licence class are not cross-checked *(probed)*
findings.response: The v2 schema and projection enforce a conservative public-export boundary: only author_open with an allowed open licence can produce public rows. third_party_restricted and unknown cannot carry a licence or publishable layers, including knowledge. Private restricted packages remain valid. Separately authored derivatives need their own artifact and rights decision.
verification: RightsAndProjectionTests cover forged licences, restricted knowledge, unknown class and valid private packages with no public rows.
findings.remaining_limit: Producer fail-closed rule implementing DEC-AUP-0173, not a legal claim that all original derivatives are prohibited. Rights ownership remains externally authenticated input.

findings.title: `knowledge_ready` accepts a review whose result is `unsupported` *(probed)*
findings.response: knowledge_ready requires a supported review from a declared independent human or blind agent distinct from the producer, explicit independence basis, complete object/relation coverage, exact byte bindings and reviewed status for every record. Negative, partial, same-session, same-identity and stale reviews cannot establish readiness.
verification: ReviewReadinessTests cover negative/partial reviews, identity separation, scope, hashes and candidate/rejected records.
findings.remaining_limit: Declared identity separation and review binding are checked; actual authenticity, blinding and semantic quality remain trust inputs. Fixture reviews are explicitly synthetic.

findings.title: Status model promises transition rules but gives only one
findings.response: The status model now defines separate vocabularies, actors and legal transitions for execution and artifacts, terminal states, quarantine/reassessment, append-only observations and conservative freshness/eligibility projections. Storage and scientific status are not inferred from a general positive status.
verification: Cross-specification comparison of canonical dimensions and transition tables; profile fixtures reject noncanonical check values.
findings.remaining_limit: Architectural transition obligations are specified; no deployed distributed state machine is certified.

findings.title: Publication guard and "generation" are required in three specs but never defined
findings.response: Generation is monotone and never reissued within a head namespace, including rollback, restart and revocation. Publication must atomically compare head generation, every material dependency epoch and authority/policy before replacing the head and advancing generation. A separate dependency check followed by head-only CAS is explicitly insufficient.
verification: PublicationRaceTests cover stale workers, revocation, stale dependency with current head, omitted authority, namespace mismatch, ABA rollback, concurrent publishers and overflow.

Integration exposed dependency-counter exhaustion followed by a refused revocation and an incorrectly accepted publication. The guard now rejects exhausted dependency counters; a separate regression covers both old and fresh read sets and the last dependency increment.
findings.remaining_limit: The local model implements the epoch/revocation subset. Output-specific grants, semantic validity, build checks, persistence and distributed consistency require separate implementation evidence.

findings.title: Two admission vocabularies and three names for the admission authority
findings.response: Current documents consistently use Knowledge Contract admission runtime and the outcomes success/partial/refused/failed/unresolved. ready denotes lifecycle or availability. kc2_admission and other historical identifiers are explicitly legacy names, not current runtime/publication version claims.
verification: API editor cross-checked the status table and book-package/2 mapping; historical raw spellings retained.
findings.remaining_limit: Existing deployed/private API responses are not claimed to have changed.

findings.title: Package status is claimed to be "derived" but the derivation is partial and leaves reachable states with no legal status *(probed)*
findings.response: Package status now follows a total first-match decision table: mismatch, bibliographic-only, missing conversion, absent semantics, complete readiness, then partial_pilot. Reviewed but unverified or partially extracted packages have explicit non-ready outcomes. Structural contradictions still fail validation.
verification: test_total_decision_table_over_all_status_dimensions checks 3,240 combinations and all six statuses; regressions cover reviewed/unverified, reviewed/partial and bibliographic mismatch.
findings.remaining_limit: Classification totality is not evidence of source fidelity or semantic correctness; knowledge_ready is not runtime admission.

findings.title: Requirements are not identifiable, so "state which requirements it satisfies" cannot be done
findings.response: Normative sentences in the eleven specifications and API appendix now have stable per-document IDs and a machine-readable requirement register. The checker detects missing/duplicate/wrong-prefix IDs and stale registry content, while distinguishing finite automated examples from implementation-specific obligations.
verification: python -B tools/check_requirement_register.py returned REQUIREMENT_REGISTER_PASS requirements=283.
findings.remaining_limit: An indexed requirement or linked regression is not a full conformance certificate. New normative text needs new IDs and register regeneration.

findings.title: No wire format: the README promises "implementable obligations" that two teams cannot interoperate on
findings.response: Added bounded observation, dependency-event and profile-advertisement wire profiles with JSON Schema 2020-12, exact examples, strict JSON, typed revisions, scoped checks, monotone epochs, byte hash domains and migration limits. All remaining full-contract models explicitly state architectural rather than universal wire interoperability.
verification: ExchangeTests cover three families, exact-byte hashes, malformed JSON, pinned inapplicability rules, calendar dates, monotone events and profile advertisement; duplicate keys, NaN/Infinity and 1e999 overflow are rejected.
findings.remaining_limit: No universal full-contract schema, deployed endpoint or cross-vendor certification is claimed; interoperability is limited to the named profiles.

findings.title: Rendered knowledge layer drops conditions, operator scopes, source position and attribution without a loss account *(probed)*
findings.response: Knowledge rendering now preserves complete objects and relations as literal JSON, including conditions, scopes, operators, source positions, origins, anchors and assessment bindings. Headings are a convenience view rather than a lossy replacement.
verification: test_full_records_survive_rendering_and_cannot_inject_heading round-trips complete records.
findings.remaining_limit: Preserving serialized fields does not prove that extraction captured all source meaning.

findings.title: Markdown injection lets generated text forge the "Author's statement" label *(probed)*
findings.response: Untrusted fields are serialized inside adaptive JSON code fences longer than any embedded backtick run. Trusted origin labels stay outside the literal payload, so generated headings and HTML cannot forge author attribution in the renderer output.
verification: Full-record rendering regression includes backticks, fabricated headings and HTML payloads.
findings.remaining_limit: Downstream renderers must preserve code-block semantics rather than reinterpret JSON string values as Markdown.

findings.title: `pass` with `unknown` or zero checks contradicts the status model *(probed)*
findings.response: Extraction pass now requires at least one applicable passing check, unique IDs, no failed/unknown checks and consistent expected/seen values. not_applicable requires a stated basis and cannot make an empty or all-inapplicable set pass.
verification: Tests cover empty/unknown/failed checks and missing inapplicability basis.
findings.remaining_limit: The validator checks existence of a basis, not the semantic truth of an inapplicability conclusion.

findings.title: `asset_text` edits are accepted without any check, and the spec never defines them *(probed)*
findings.response: Removed undefined asset_text edits. Only readable_md edits use the reversible ledger; accepted edits without converted document/readable material fail. Exact-byte, UTF-8, newline, range, overlap and reversal controls are retained.
verification: test_asset_text_and_edits_without_document_are_rejected and existing byte-ledger regressions.
findings.remaining_limit: Asset-text correction needs a separately specified future profile; no automatic conversion of unsupported edits.

findings.title: Staleness rule is keyed to an undefined edit state and to producer-declared dependencies
findings.response: Explicit edit-state semantics and anchor-overlap detection invalidate affected objects independently of producer dependency declarations. Recovery requires an edit-specific supported bound reassessment. Relations cannot remain reviewed with stale/rejected endpoints.
verification: Accepted-edit overlap test omits producer dependencies then exercises explicit reassessment; rejected-endpoint relation test.
findings.remaining_limit: Overlap is conservative. Semantic effects outside recorded coordinate/dependency scope require review; arbitrary semantic closure is not inferred.

findings.title: Integrity `verified` is a producer assertion that gates `knowledge_ready`
findings.response: Verified/mismatch integrity requires method, observer, timestamp and expected/observed digests with cross-file consistency checks. Builder records disclose caller-supplied expected-digest authority limitations.
verification: Integrity observation/digest regression plus negative fixture missing observer.
findings.remaining_limit: Internal consistency does not authenticate expected digest origin or observer; consumers must verify the trust basis.

findings.title: Time model: soft deadline, TTL class, staleness bound and "invalid chronology" are undefined
findings.response: Defined soft/hard TTL and deadline classes, conservative interval bounds, expiry equality, maximum-age comparison and invalid chronology. Soft staleness requires revalidation unless explicit serve_stale permission exists; refresh failure cannot renew evidence.
verification: Manual boundary review covers age, equality at expiry, failed refresh, invalid/overlapping intervals and seven reuse decisions.
findings.remaining_limit: No production clock/timing implementation is supplied; operational conformance requires its own uncertainty/policy tests.

findings.title: Parallel vocabularies for the same dimension across specs
findings.response: Canonical dimension tokens govern run phases, availability, eligibility, impact, search assurance, coverage, operation outcomes and reuse decisions. Legacy terms have mappings; unsupported records its scope rather than adding a parallel token; ready is not an outcome.
verification: Cross-document vocabulary comparison and schema enums for the bounded subset.
findings.remaining_limit: Historical evidence keeps original labels and measurements with explicit compatibility mappings.

findings.title: Book-package facets claim consistency with semantic types but diverge in vocabulary
findings.response: Book v2 facets distinguish hypothesizes/presumes, add condition/exception/order operator families, retain explicit scope and support structured_data representation. Cardinality and unknown/known-empty meanings are stated.
verification: Facet regression and regenerated positive/negative fixtures.
findings.remaining_limit: Representational classification still needs semantic review; legacy v1 records are not automatically reclassified.

findings.title: Anchor/format table in the spec differs from the validator's mapping
findings.response: The source-format/anchor table matches validation, including pptx. Archives are opaque source identities with no semantic member-coordinate or converted-document profile; unsupported archive interpretation fails rather than receiving invented anchors.
verification: Archive/pptx mapping regression and existing anchor fixtures.
findings.remaining_limit: Archive extraction/member coordinates remain explicitly unsupported pending a separate profile.

findings.title: Profile "required" flag is producer-controlled; a constraint can be downgraded to optional
findings.response: Constraint mandatoriness derives from trusted request/policy independently of a producer required flag. Unknown constraint relevance blocks use. Only established irrelevant opaque extensions may be ignored, and conflict-resolution authority must be authenticated.
verification: Manual downgrade, unknown-extension and unauthenticated-resolver threat-case trace against the revised obligations.
findings.remaining_limit: The architecture does not supply a general policy engine or authentication service.

findings.title: Lowercase "must" carries central requirements; the appendix and book package have no BCP 14 keywords at all
findings.response: Central obligations use BCP 14 keywords with stable IDs. The book profile and API proposed-delivery/gate sections declare normative scope; the observed read-interface inventory remains informative.
verification: Requirement checker validates 283 requirements; API editor confirmed 35 numbered API clauses and intended BCP 14 scope.
findings.remaining_limit: Keywords identify obligations; they do not establish deployed service conformance.

findings.title: "Descriptor" is used normatively but defined only circularly
findings.response: Descriptor identity now has a concrete component table for operation, sources/revisions, semantic requirements, constraints, authority/policy, projections, parameters, toolchain and dependencies. Each comparison is exact or uses separately evidenced compatibility/entailment; a hash alone is insufficient.
verification: Manual component-by-component reuse review and exact hash-domain controls in the bounded profile.
findings.remaining_limit: The full descriptor is architectural; universal serialization is not claimed outside the named wire subset.

findings.title: `package_id` allows characters the exporter path pattern rejects *(probed)*
findings.response: Active v2 identity uses a readable exporter-compatible package_slug and separate release_id. Colon-bearing and opaque numbered aliases fail. Builder and synthetic fixtures were migrated together.
verification: Package-slug, builder opaque-slug and path-safety regressions.
findings.remaining_limit: Breaking v2 change: historical package_id fields stay in immutable v1 history, without silent rewriting.

findings.title: Registry naming ban is not enforced
findings.response: Root added publication checker rejection of opaque numbered canonical slugs/titles, including r1, r10, p09 and numeric-only names. Legacy artifact names remain explicitly outside the current catalogue.
verification: test_opaque_numbered_names_cannot_enter_the_current_catalog and test_opaque_numbered_title_is_rejected; root owns final rerun.
findings.remaining_limit: A lexical check cannot prove that a name communicates useful meaning; editorial review remains necessary.

findings.title: Empty known list allowed for some facets but not others
findings.response: Known-empty semantics are specified per facet. Classification facets requiring a nonempty known set differ from a measured absence of operators, conditions or references. Every object covered by the package review must name that review in assessment_refs.
verification: Facet known-empty regression and test_known_empty_assessment_refs_cannot_deny_a_named_package_review.
findings.remaining_limit: The validator distinguishes declarations but cannot prove a claimed empty observation complete.

findings.title: `candidate_projection` does not require a validated package or a publishable status
findings.response: candidate_projection takes a directory, creates an isolated exact-byte snapshot, validates it and renders from that same snapshot. Invalid, unavailable and non-open packages produce no public proposal. Caller-supplied manifest/rendering pairs are no longer accepted.
verification: Projection tests cover invalid package, raw-input injection and self-bound rendering.
findings.remaining_limit: The result is only an export proposal; it does not edit an allowlist, grant admission, publish an index or authenticate author_open.

findings.title: `presented_as_author` semantics for `author_statement` undefined
findings.response: For author_statement, presented_as_author=true means asserted verbatim attribution and false means attributed paraphrase. Non-author/generated origins stay false with explicit generated labels. A redundant schema condition was removed.
verification: Lossless-rendering regression and existing attribution/origin negative fixtures.
findings.remaining_limit: The flag records a producer claim; source fidelity requires independent evidence.

findings.title: API appendix: repository identity and release-gate receipt unspecified
findings.response: API identity is now tied to observed source_revision plus citation.canonical_url. A separate KCIndexReleaseReceipt/v1 operator profile defines normalized repository_url, document hashes, build identity, query/fetch readbacks, supersession and six gate checks; no deployed repository_url field is invented.
verification: Studies editor inspected site adapter cdca604245165bbec80ce3624fdc65e9cbde6a01; validated Draft 2020-12 schema with 2,187 state/decision combinations, six missing-check and five traversal cases.

Persistent tools/test_index_release_receipt.py controls cover all 2,187 declared check-state/decision combinations, each omitted check and malformed paths/identities. Explicit date assertion is exercised on UTC-seconds fixtures; full RFC 3339 support and semantic joins are not certified by these shape checks.
findings.remaining_limit: Shape/decision validation does not establish semantic joins, live API data, deployment, index state or corpus authority. No production receipt was fabricated.

findings.title: "Conflicting adoption decisions" is a required test without a defined expected result
findings.response: Conflicting adoption decisions explicitly block affected use until authenticated resolution or justified narrower scope. Unknown impact yields unknown eligibility and unresolved outcome; established prohibition yields blocked impact and refusal.
verification: Manual acceptance-case review of conflicting authorities, unknown relevance, known prohibition and authorized resolution.
findings.remaining_limit: The operational authority/resolution service remains implementation-specific; unresolved conflict is not declared harmless.
